questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Jacobian?
questions.answer: A Jacobian measures how a coordinate change stretches small area or volume elements. It is the factor that makes integrals preserve the actual size of regions after changing variables.

questions.prompt: What does \(u,v\) mean in Jacobian?
questions.answer: In Jacobian, \(u,v\) means new variables.

questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for Jacobian.
questions.answer:
The jacobian determinant is
\[J=\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}x_u&x_v\\y_u&y_v\end{vmatrix}\]
Use it only after the symbols in the formula have been identified for the specific jacobian problem.

questions.prompt: Compute the Jacobian for \(x=r\cos\theta\), \(y=r\sin\theta\).
questions.answer: The derivative matrix is \[\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-r\sin\theta\\sin\theta&r\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}\] Its determinant is \[r\cos^2\theta+r\sin^2\theta=r\] Therefore \(dA=r\,dr\,d\theta\).

questions.prompt: If \(x=2u\) and \(y=3v\), what is the area scale factor?
questions.answer: The Jacobian matrix is diagonal: \[\begin{pmatrix}2&0\0&3\end{pmatrix}\] Its determinant is \(6\), so \(dA=6\,du\,dv\). Areas are stretched by a factor of \(6\).
